pr_title: Fix `RestoreDefaultValueButton` not behaving correctly on number types
pr_body:
- [x] Depends on https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/pull/4554
- [x] Depends on framework bump
- [x] Depends on ppy/osu-framework#4568
- [x] Depends on framework bump

Closes #13649
pr_comments:
Yeah... looks to be caused by `SettingsSourceAttributeTest` providing a regular `Bindable` to the `CustomSettingsControl`'s control `Current`, and `SettingsItem` (inherited by the settings control) attempted to bind that to the `RestoreDefaultValueButton`, resulting in that failure.

I'm not yet sure whether `Bindable`s are allowed to be bound together with `BindableNumber`s, `BindableNumberWithCurrent` seems to enforce not doing that and directly casts the given current bindable to `BindableNumber`...

If they shouldn't be allowed to be bound together, maybe that should be shown clearly by an exception framework-side when attempting to bind bindables to ones which are `!bindable.GetType().IsAssignableFrom(GetType())`, or at least not make `BindableNumberWithCurrent` directly cast and instead throw an exception.

Will fix the test here to make a `BindableInt` instead, and double-check the existing cases to avoid hitting another similar crash.

Hmm, seems this can also occur on a `SettingsDropdown` with a number type...

Starting to think it might be a better and easier choice to take the bindable instance directly and manage the event binding internally and call it a day. @bdach thoughts?

> take the bindable instance directly and manage the event binding internally

I don't know what this means, so I can't either agree or disagree without seeing actual source. The current approach does seems wrong/no longer viable from what I understand, however.

Bit weird that that's only coming out now, but alas (did you not try running tests after applying your changes at all?)

> I don't know what this means, so I can't either agree or disagree without seeing actual source.

Here's a quick commit for that: https://github.com/ppy/osu/commit/612ed6353c909da3d1099222795d8a3abf49a2d0

I *think* that may be fine, if a bit dangerous. One thing I can say for sure is that now that that code is holding onto external bindable references you probably also need to explicitly unbind on disposal/`UnbindAllBindables` to avoid a leak...?

Good point, that also means the direct bindable reference can get unbound on drawable disposal, which is not wanted... should be resolved by holding a bound copy to it instead, so it gets unbound correctly on drawable disposal.

Depends on a [framework-side PR](https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/pull/4568) for fixing a bug with `GetBoundCopy()` calls on `BindableWithCurrent` classes, however.
I'm not confident in reviewing this without a more in-depth explanation of what the failure mode was.

The issue this PR was attempting to fix in multiple ways was that the `BindableWithCurrent` returns incorrect `IsDefault` values due to not having the concept of a "precision" when binding to a `BindableNumber`, as in the comment above.

This PR originally attempted to fix that by creating either `BindableWithCurrent` or `BindableNumberWithCurrent` depending on the type, but that turned out to cause failures due to `BindableNumberWithCurrent` forcing any bindable assigned to its `Current` property to be of type `BindableNumber<T>` (by direct cast), which is not necessarily the case (talked about it in-depth [here](https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/13701#issuecomment-873165932)).

Therefore I ended up with just removing all the `BindableWithCurrent` logic and did the bindable current management manually instead.

I'm only considering this as a temporary solution for now, I am not completely sure what the final solution should be, this is a flaw in the way `BindableWithCurrent` and `BindableNumberWithCurrent` are designed right now and will require reconsideration framework-side (stuff like whether bindable number and regular bindable can be bound together, and remove that constraint from `BindableNumberWithCurrent.Current` to allow using the original fix, etc.)
At very least, this needs an inline comment around the `Current` handling to explain why it's being done differently to everywhere else.
Now that I look at this, this probably needs a test scene... will write one quickly.

I've added a test case for this, but it's sorta flaky given that the values used for testing are ones that just underflow for some reason, can't figure out a solid way to retrieve underflowing numbers. @bdach thoughts? unless this is actually not deterministic?

Floating-point math *is* deterministic, but the .NET team gives no guarantees that its .NET implementation will be stable across .NET releases. So this test case is sorta weak in that respect but I guess it makes *some* sense.

Adjusted it slightly but otherwise am fine with it.

I'm very hesitant to approve of this without going back an understanding the full path we took to get here (ie. the implications of *not* using `BindableWithCurrent`). Especially as `UnbindAll` is potentially unbinding externally bound events/bindings that, as far as I can tell never used to be the case, and could cause critical and hard to track failures.

The unbind is ran on a copy. It's not that much different from `BindableWithCurrent` itself, except for the fact that that stores a reference to the currently-bound bindable and does `UnbindFrom()`, and not `UnbindAll()`.

I'm not sure what else there is left to explain about why `BindableWithCurrent` cannot be used.

I see. My next question would be: we're fixing this locally here, but could it not break in the same way elsewhere with usage of `BindableWithCurrent`?

And I guess from https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/13701#issuecomment-875305913, this is only supposed to be a temporary fix? Seems okay I guess.

It could, yes. As it stands `BindableWithCurrent` is manually duplicating the class hierarchy of `Bindable` which breaks down in generic cases like this in which you do not necessarily know what the exact type of the original bindable is, and therefore don't know what the desired semantics (in this case wrt `Default`) are.

For 100% automatic operation `BindableNumberWithCurrent` should no longer exist and `BindableWithCurrent` would have to be able to switch its underlying bindable type on the fly (consider assigning `Bindable<float>` Vs `BindableFloat` to it). That also opens up the question of how to access the properties of the derived in such a case (`Precision` etc.)

issue_context.title: Some default CS values show the "revert to default" button in the Difficulty Adjust mod
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** For some reason, the `Circle Size` value in the `Difficulty Adjust` mod's customization has the "revert to default" button even if it's already the default (but only with some specific CS values). I noticed it in [this map](https://osu.ppy.sh/beatmapsets/927758#osu) (in the last two highest difficulties).

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43073074/123237336-dfa62280-d4dd-11eb-949b-911a1923799d.mp4

**osu!lazer version:** `2021.623.0`
comments: @PercyDan54 it may well be, but i fail to see how a screenshot of chrome devtools showing js behaviour relates to c# behaviour or this issue. have you actually debugged this?

> @PercyDan54 it may well be, but i fail to see how a screenshot of chrome devtools showing js behaviour relates to c# behaviour or this issue. have you actually debugged this?

Haven't debugged but I think it's somehow related to this, since he said `only specific values` is affected.

But here's my guess:
https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/blob/d02d15db853021669dca5461df5ad1dd91d378be/osu.Framework/Bindables/BindableNumber.cs#L79
Here a float is casted to double, causing this precision loss.

And another screenshot with C# interactive:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/50285552/123257310-93ca9c00-d524-11eb-9ae3-5f2de9eeaabf.png)

I've *actually* debugged this. `BindableNumber`s handle precision issues correctly. The *actual* problem is that `RestoreDefaultValueButton` always uses a `BindableWithCurrent<T>`, while it should be using `BindableNumberWithCurrent<T>` for numeric controls, which in turn leads it to use the wrong base implementation of `IsDefault` rather than the correct one which comes from `BindableNumber` et al.

@PercyDan54 please refrain from posting untested theories about root causes of a bug in the future if you have not actually debugged and root-caused them properly.

Looks to be regressed by #12728 indirectly, since now `RestoreDefaultValueButton` uses a `BindableWithCurrent`, while previously it accesses the bindable instance directly.

One solution I can see here is overriding `IsDefault` in `BindableWithCurrent` to point to the current's one, which seems to be the cleanest out of the other ways I thought about (such as not using `BindableWithCurrent` to begin with). Would like to hear your thoughts on this.

by "the current's one" you mean the public `Current`, or the private `currentBound`? because i don't think the former will help (because, again, it's a `Bindable<float>`, and not a `BindableFloat`, and therefore has no precision logic in `IsDefault`), and i'm not sure the further should be allowed because it just makes things messy (different properties of `BindableWithCurrent` will actually access different bindable instances).

i think i'd rather have framework hook up/create the "correct" type automatically somehow, maybe via a factory method (`BindableWithCurrent.Create<T>()` which returns `BindableNumberWithCurrent` when `T` allows it)?

I mean the private `currentBound` of course, `Current` points to `this` anyways.

Having a method that constructs either `BindableWithCurrent` or `BindableNumberWithCurrent` is also something I've considered, but it can't really work since `T` must have certain interfaces implemented to be able to use on `BindableNumberWithCurrent`, unless it's fine to do it via reflection? (if that's even possible)

I would see it being done via typechecks on `typeof(T)`, which are optimised out by the JIT in the case of generics. Refer to `BindableNumber`'s implementation of `DefaultMinValue` et al. I suppose you _would_ still have to use `Activator.CreateInstance()` to construct an instance even after that.

review_comments: It sure looks like `UnbindAll` won't unregister from `DefaultChanged` to me (see [link 1](https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/blob/d6d14ce4723def41e5b4af7216824752882b4d49/osu.Framework/Bindables/Bindable.cs#L363-L370), [link 2](https://github.com/ppy/osu-framework/blob/d6d14ce4723def41e5b4af7216824752882b4d49/osu.Framework/Bindables/Bindable.cs#L335-L339)).
That looks like a very bad oversight... don't think anything would've unbound them and references were leaked for those which used them all the time.
The PR should be fine to go as this was the case previously anyways, and this PR doesn't worsen anything in that aspect.
Think this might need a `IsLoaded` guard still, and the `LoadComplete()` stuff might need to go back in? Not sure.
It's sorta unnecessary since it's already injected with a `Current` once created in `SettingsItem`, but no point in removing it.
